title: CAP: advanced salivary gland cancer
indication_text: Advanced salivary gland cancer, after specialist review of histology, treatment choices and goals.
purpose: This treatment aims to slow cancer growth and help control symptoms. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your situation.
cycle_display: Day 1 every 21 days; up to 6 cycles
schedule_label: Day 1 every 21 days; up to 6 cycles
schedule_summary: Doxorubicin 50 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² on Day 1, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects.
administration_text: Doxorubicin is given slowly into a vein over about 15 minutes, cisplatin over 2 hours, then cyclophosphamide over 30 minutes. Cisplatin requires prescribed intravenous fluids before and after treatment, so the visit takes longer than the drug infusion times. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage around the line.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests during treatment. Review hydration, blood salts, hearing, tingling or numbness, heart symptoms, mouth care and prior toxicities before further doses. Record lifetime anthracycline exposure; the source doxorubicin limit is 450 mg/m².

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body into compounds that damage DNA. Bladder irritation is one reason for a clear hydration plan.
agents.watch: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, infection, bleeding and anaemia
Sickness, mouth ulcers, diarrhoea, tiredness and hair loss
Cyclophosphamide-related bladder irritation and blood in urine
Fertility effects, pregnancy risk and rare later second cancers

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages DNA and interferes with repair
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care.
agents.watch: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, infection, bleeding and anaemia
Sickness, mouth ulcers, diarrhoea, tiredness and hair loss
Doxorubicin-related heart damage and tissue injury if it leaks outside a vein
Fertility effects, pregnancy risk and rare later second cancers

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links within DNA that impede copying. The kidneys, hearing and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, infection, bleeding and anaemia
Sickness, mouth ulcers, diarrhoea, tiredness and hair loss
Cisplatin-related kidney damage, low blood salts, hearing loss and nerve damage
Fertility effects, pregnancy risk and rare later second cancers

Report breathlessness, chest symptoms, hearing changes or tingling promptly. Heart, hearing and nerve injury can persist.
Use prescribed support. Report persistent diarrhoea or vomiting, inability to drink, blood or severe abdominal pain.
Report reduced urine, swelling or poor fluid intake; keep blood and urine tests.
Hair loss may occur. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage at the infusion site.
Discuss fertility preservation, contraception, pregnancy and breastfeeding before starting.

evidence.title: What the evidence can tell you
evidence.intro: Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.
evidence.population: Advanced salivary gland cancer, after specialist review of histology, treatment choices and goals.
evidence.comparison: Limited evidence for this specific regimen and setting
evidence.interpretation: The NCCP CAP regimen draws on small salivary gland cancer studies. Salivary gland cancers include different histologies, and this evidence does not provide a reliable personalised survival gain. Discuss the aim of symptom control, chance of tumour response, burdens of treatment and histology-specific alternatives.
limitations: Small studies and mixed tumour groups limit certainty.
Other doses or combinations cannot be assumed equivalent.
